title: A Little Too Generous
summary: You're allowed to read log files as root. Only log files. Surely that can't go wrong?
briefing:
NovaTech has hired you for a **penetration test**: an agreed, written-down attempt to break in, so weaknesses are found before criminals find them.

You get a normal account on novatech-srv – with one extra. The operations team often needs to read log files that only root may open, so Sam the admin added a **sudo rule**: you may run one specific command as root.

Sam is sure it's safe. Your goal from the contract: read `/root/flag.txt`, a file only root can open.
objective: Find out what sudo lets you run, and use that rule to read /root/flag.txt.
debrief:
Root! The rule was meant to allow `cat /var/log/*` – but in sudo rules `*` matches *any* text. `/var/log/../../root/flag.txt` starts with `/var/log/`, so sudo said yes, and the two `..` then walked straight up and into `/root`.

There was even a second way in: `sudo cat /var/log/syslog /root/flag.txt` also matches, because `*` matches the space and the extra file name too.

Getting more rights than you were given is called **privilege escalation**, and too-generous sudo rules are one of its most common causes. The lesson for NovaTech: avoid wildcards in sudo rules, give people only exactly what they need – and for reading logs, add them to a log-reading group instead.
hints: `sudo` runs one command as root – but only commands that the sudo rules allow. Start with `sudo -l` to see your rule. Then read it very carefully: what exactly does it allow, and what does `*` match?

Your rule allows `cat` on anything matching `/var/log/*`. In sudo rules `*` matches **any** text – including `..`, which means "go up one folder". A path can start with `/var/log/` and still end up somewhere completely different.

lines: # /etc/sudoers – who may run which commands as root.
# Ops asked for a way to read the logs without root. Done! – Sam
Defaults        env_reset
root    ALL=(ALL) ALL
user    ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/cat /var/log/*
PENETRATION TEST – CONTRACT (summary)
Client:   NovaTech
Target:   novatech-srv
Tester:   you
You are allowed to try to get root on novatech-srv using the account
you were given. Proof of success: the contents of /root/flag.txt.
Not allowed: deleting or changing anything, or touching other servers.
Signed: Alex (CEO), Sam (admin)
